steps.name: V-1: with an owner that cannot create roles the start command stops before the API starts
steps.detail: roles refused: V-1 failed: plain_owner cannot create roles. Stop: do not run the API as the owner (docs/operations/RENDER_DEPLOYMENT.md §V-1)

steps.name: the start command, as written in the Blueprint, prepares an empty database as an owner that is not a superuser — creating the two runtime roles — and brings the API up in production, demonstration mode
steps.detail: 41 migrations · authMode demo · roles created ×2 · 18 variables from the Blueprint · PostgreSQL 16.15 (Ubuntu 16.15-0ubuntu0.24.04.1)

steps.name: the deployment check passes against it: permissions, unauthorized access, isolation, persistence, cross-origin, reset

a restart: the same command runs again as the same owner — the role step finds the roles and sets their passwords — and changes nothing; a sandbox opened before it opens with its key after it and reads the same record; a session issued before it is still good
steps.detail: stopped, nothing answering, started again · roles: password set ×2 · session from the key 200 · same thread true · earlier session 200 · 41 migrations, 4 sandboxes, unchanged

steps.name: the self-check: off as declared, nothing runs; switched on, the deployment check runs inside the service against its own address and its lines are in the log
the database holds sandboxes and nothing else: no other tenant, nobody with a password or a provider subject
the runtime roles are not the owner and can do nothing but sign in: the API's role cannot read the sandbox table, change the setting, or create a tenant
steps.detail: permission denied ×3 of 3 · roles with no attribute but LOGIN: 2 of 2 · rooms visible without a tenant: 0

steps.name: the privilege list in the image is exactly what the migrations produce on an empty database
a plain pg_dump with the owner’s URL is refused: row-level security is forced on the owner, so the export has to be the platform’s
steps.detail: pg_dump: error: query failed: ERROR:  query would be affected by row-level security policy for table "acceptance_criterion"

steps.name: recovery: an export made with the platform’s privileges restores into an empty database as the owner; migrations, rows, forced row-level security and every audit chain are verified against the source; on the copy as restored the service is unhealthy and refuses, the runtime role cannot repair the privileges and the owner’s repair makes them equal to the source’s; the API then serves the restored copy and a sandbox opened before the export opens with its key and reads the same thread
steps.detail: RV-01 PASS · RV-02 PASS · RV-03 PASS · RV-04 PASS · RV-05 PASS · 4864 rows, 7 chains · objects not the owner’s: 0 · API on the copy true · same thread true · recorded after the export: on the source v2, in the copy v1 (lost, as it must be) · export 0.2 s (203 KiB), restore 0.8 s, verify 2.6 s, serving again 16.1 s

steps.name: the verification is not a formality: one audit row changed and one row removed in the restored copy are both reported
steps.detail: RV-02 FAIL: 245 sealed rows in 7 chains · 1 hashes differ · 0 broken links · 0 gaps · 0 rows not yet s | RV-04 FAIL: 4863 rows in 80 tables (source 4864) · tables that differ: app.field_mounting 3→2 · chain heads the same

steps.name: rotating the three secrets is a restart with new values: every session issued before stops, the old database password no longer connects, and a sandbox still opens with its key and reads the same thread
steps.detail: earlier session 401 · session from the key 200, same thread true · old role password refused · new one accepted

steps.name: an expired sandbox: its key opens nothing, a session issued before stops, the visitor is told why, and its records are kept
steps.detail: session 401 · key 401 “the sandbox is unknown, closed or expired, or the key is not right” · 34 audit rows and the room still in the database

recovery.lost: whatever was recorded after the export was made: here one mounting (version 2 on the source, version 1 in the copy)
recovery.measuredOn: this workstation, a local PostgreSQL cluster; not the platform

smoke.detail: status ok · authMode demo · release f615a99dbaac (staging) · migrations 41

smoke.detail: sign-in 404 · public form 404 · no token 401 · made-up token 401 bad token signature

smoke.title: a sandbox opens with a key, sixteen synthetic people and two installed rooms, one of them the flagship lecture theatre by its canonical identifier; its first session is the installer’s

smoke.title: correct permissions: the installer records a mounting and a field move; the systems engineer approves the move

smoke.detail: 403 designer may not record how a device is mounted (needs work.evidence or field.scan) | own move 403 | 403 installer may not move a room to COMMISSIONING (needs plan.compile) | 403 | 403 | gate 422

smoke.detail: wrong key 401 · unknown 401 · B’s key 401 · architect/founder/secadmin 400/400/400

smoke.detail: same code, two rooms: true · B sees its own (mounted 0) · B→A read 404 · A→B read 404 · B→A write 404

smoke.title: a new session made from the key alone, as a different person, reads the same field record and thread
smoke.detail: mounted 1 · approved moves 1 · as built FM-0001 · refusals on the record 4

the demo site’s origin is allowed, with PUT; any other origin is not

database: a PostgreSQL 16.15 (Ubuntu 16.15-0ubuntu0.24.04.1) cluster created for this run and removed after it; owner: not a superuser, may create roles
limits: No TLS in the rehearsal cluster (PGSSLMODE rehearsed as disable); no Render proxy, container or free-plan sleep; the owner's attributes beyond "not a superuser, may create roles" are an assumption about the platform's user. The image build and the edge are seen only on Render.
